healthcareSystem: Government-funded healthcare system providing free or heavily subsidized care to citizens and residents. RIPAS Hospital in Bandar Seri Begawan is the main facility and is well-equipped. Private clinics supplement public care. Foreign visitors pay modest fees. Healthcare quality is good with modern equipment funded by oil wealth.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is good by Southeast Asian standards, funded by Brunei's oil wealth. RIPAS Hospital is modern and well-equipped. Specialist care is available for many conditions. For highly complex cases, the government sends citizens to Singapore or Malaysia; tourists may also consider evacuation to Singapore. English is widely spoken in medical settings alongside Malay.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-9pm daily. Hospital pharmacies available 24/7. Guardian and other chain pharmacies in shopping malls have extended hours.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are well-stocked with common medications. English is widely spoken. Note that alcohol-based medications may not be available due to Brunei's alcohol ban. Prices are reasonable. Guardian pharmacy chain is reliable and found in major shopping areas.
prescriptionRules: Prescription requirements are enforced. Antibiotics require a prescription. Standard OTC medications are available without prescription. Controlled substances require valid documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly controlled under Brunei's drug laws, which are extremely harsh. Carry doctor's letter and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly illegal. Brunei has a zero-tolerance drug policy with severe penalties including death penalty for trafficking.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Some cough medicines containing codeine are restricted. Carry prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Alcohol-based medications
restrictedMeds.note: Alcohol is banned in Brunei. Medications with alcohol content may be questioned at customs.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter for all controlled medications. Brunei has extremely strict drug laws — penalties are severe. Keep all medications in original pharmacy packaging. Declare medications at customs if in doubt.

travelInsurance.tips: Recommended though healthcare costs are moderate. Useful for medical evacuation to Singapore for complex cases. Public hospital costs for foreigners are reasonable but private care is more expensive.

required: Yellow Fever (only if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for most travelers. Yellow fever certificate required from endemic areas only. Routine vaccinations should be current.

waterNotes: Tap water in Brunei is safe to drink. The water treatment system is modern and well-maintained. Bottled water is widely available but not necessary in urban areas.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety standards are good. Brunei has strict halal food regulations. Street food and restaurant food are generally safe. Rice dishes, nasi katok (chicken with rice and sambal), and fresh seafood are staples. No alcohol is served anywhere in Brunei. Night markets in Gadong offer excellent local food.
medicalTourismNote: Brunei is not a medical tourism destination. Citizens are typically sent to Singapore or Malaysia for complex treatments. The country is visited for its mosques, rainforest, and cultural experiences.
metaDescription: Health guide for Brunei: modern hospitals, strict drug laws, pharmacy tips, alcohol ban, vaccinations, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Raja Isteri Pengiran Anak Saleha Hospital (RIPAS)
hospitals.notes: Main government hospital. Modern, well-equipped facility. 24/7 emergency department. English and Malay spoken. The primary hospital for the entire country.

hospitals.name: Jerudong Park Medical Centre (JPMC)
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Jerudong (near the Empire Hotel resort area)
hospitals.notes: Private specialist hospital. Higher standard of comfort. Used by expatriates and visitors. Modern diagnostic equipment.

hospitals.name: Suri Seri Begawan Hospital
hospitals.notes: District hospital serving the Belait oil-producing region. Good standard of care.

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available. Government dental clinics and private dental practices in Bandar Seri Begawan.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is of reasonable quality. RIPAS Hospital has a dental department. Private dental clinics offer comfortable, modern care. Most dentists speak English.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Visit RIPAS Hospital dental department or a private dental clinic in the capital. JPMC also has dental services.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited. Some private counselors in Bandar Seri Begawan speak English. RIPAS Hospital has psychiatric services.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are available but limited. Cultural stigma around mental health exists. RIPAS Hospital has a psychiatric unit. Private counseling is available in the capital.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is developing. Newer buildings and the capital's main attractions have basic accessibility features. Older buildings may lack wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: RIPAS Hospital and JPMC have wheelchair access and modern facilities. Elevators available in both hospitals.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Public buses are not fully accessible. Taxis can accommodate some needs. The capital is relatively flat and navigable. Water village (Kampong Ayer) is not wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Contact hotels in advance about accessibility. The Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque and Jame'Asr Hassanil Bolkiah Mosque have some accessible areas. Ulu Temburong National Park canopy walk is not accessible.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No general mask mandates. Masks may be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: COVID testing available at RIPAS Hospital and designated clinics.
covidStatus.notes: Brunei has returned to normal operations. Entry procedures are straightforward.

insuranceClaimProcess: Foreign visitors pay at government hospitals at subsidized rates. Private hospital costs are higher. Collect receipts and medical reports. RIPAS and JPMC provide documentation in English. File claims with your insurer after returning home.

commonCosts.note: Government hospital costs for foreigners are subsidized and very reasonable. Private hospital (JPMC) costs are higher. Brunei Dollar (BND) is local currency, pegged 1:1 with Singapore Dollar.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation to Singapore is standard for complex cases requiring specialist treatment not available in Brunei. Flight time is about 2 hours. Most conditions can be handled locally at RIPAS or JPMC.

pharmacyChains.name: Guardian Pharmacy
pharmacyChains.where: Shopping malls in Bandar Seri Begawan and Gadong
